title: Encores at dances: playing them right away
summary: Barnes says when the crowd claps you play the tune again right away, sometimes three times, then rest.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: I was gonna ask, I remember when Bunk used to play dances, they'd play a piece and then the people clapped right away, pick it up and play it again, repeat it like an encore. That's right. You mentioned it's best to rest in between, or is that alright to give the encore right away then?
No, no, you give the encore right away. Right away? Right away. Now, when a person calls it by a clap, if it means it, well, you'll pick it up again. But, uh...
How many times would you pick it up? As many times as they clapped it?
Well, no, you can pick it up. Sometimes they play it about three times.

But the crowd would be so heavy, yeah, they'd be so heavy on you, you'd have to play to get rid of them. Yeah, well, I should know the music stand. But sometimes the crowd would be so heavy, they'd be hollering, come on, come on, come on. Well, you'd have to play to get rid of them. Yeah. Yeah.
